title: Supreme Court of India starts AI live transcription of Constitution Bench hearings with TERES; lawyer-verified transcripts published on the court's website
summary: From 21 Feb 2023 the Supreme Court of India transcribed Constitution Bench hearings live with an AI service from TERES; 9 of 25 hearings had published transcripts by May 2023, and almost 10 matters...
account: On 21 February 2023 Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud's Constitution Bench, hearing the Maharashtra political crisis matter in Court Room 1, used AI live transcription supplied by TERES, with screens facing the lawyers showing the text; the CJI called it an experiment and said transcripts would be sent to lawyers for verification and uploaded to the Supreme Court website (LiveLaw, 21 February 2023). The Supreme Court Observer reported on 18 May 2023 that 25 Constitution Bench hearings had been held across four cases but only nine transcripts had been published (six for the marriage-equality case, three for the Maharashtra case, none for the other two), with none published in March 2023. NDTV reported on 8 December 2023 a written reply in the Lok Sabha by Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal that AI transcription had been deployed for Constitution Bench matters since February, that transcripts in almost ten main matters had been generated and published on the court's website, and that the use was on a trial basis. A Press Information Bureau feature of 11 February 2026 states that the system is being extended to regular hearing days after successful use in Constitution Bench proceedings.
purpose: The transcription was introduced to give judges, lawyers and law colleges a record of arguments and to make the court a court of record; published transcripts are that purpose.
system: TERES AI live transcription (speech-to-text) of Constitution Bench hearings
developer: TERES (named by LiveLaw as the company supplying the transcription service)
taxonomy_note: Loose fit; the transcripts are a new record of hearings for lawyers and the public, published only partially.

ratings.reason: The court gained lawyer-verified transcripts for part of its Constitution Bench hearings (9 of 25 by May 2023; almost ten matters by December 2023), on a trial basis.
Transcripts were published on the court's website for public and academic use, but only for a minority of hearings in the first months.

ai_role.statement: The AI produced the live draft; lawyers proofread before publication and, per the CJI, persons oversee overlapping speech. The published-transcript rate (36% of hearings by May 2023) shows the benefit depended on the human vetting step as much as on the recognizer.
